one_line: Shared wildfire rehearsal board combining local knowledge, public terrain evidence, bounded what-ifs, and agent assistance.
what_it_does: Runs a deterministic synthetic wildfire exercise on a live map with annotations, sector focus, scenario analysis, response staging, and human approval.
leverage_rationale: Structured domain tools let an agent inspect and mutate shared spatial exercise state precisely while preserving provenance and human authority; generic UI driving would be materially less reliable.
leverage_evidence: Six WebMCP domain tools are described.
Shared live map, labeled public/synthetic data, route constraints, and staged-but-human-approved plans are central.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a coherent, intentionally bounded workflow and the frame sheet shows the map/evidence narrative resolving into a detailed operational interface, though no end-to-end video transcript is supplied.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet visibly shows local knowledge, map evidence, AI chat, and a layered operational map.
Demo is marked alive and the board includes multiple explicit states.
impact_rationale: Wildfire planners and communities have a credible need to rehearse decisions with local context before emergencies; the shared map directly addresses fragmented handoffs.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets wildfire readiness and high-consequence exercises.
Frame sheet explicitly presents 'rehearse first' and 'every handoff loses context.'
creativity_rationale: The combination of synthetic incident rehearsal, provenance-separated public evidence, local knowledge, and bounded agent collaboration is a fresh and ambitious civic-safety interaction.
creativity_evidence: Human authority by design and visible route constraints are distinctive mechanics.
Shared map is treated as collaboration surface rather than a passive dashboard.
usability_note: Clear scenario framing and map-centered workflow; emergency-domain complexity remains substantial.
red_flags: Active incident data is synthetic; no transcript or direct agent invocation is shown.
advance_reason: High-impact, clearly differentiated shared-state workflow with credible product framing.

one_line: Visual network-stack studio that simulates traffic, quotas, failures, and bills before implementation.
what_it_does: Lets users model provider/service nodes, simulate realistic traffic over time, compare stacks, and inspect pricing-meter behavior with agent control.
leverage_rationale: Agent-accessible structured graph edits and simulations make iterative architecture/cost exploration substantially more reliable than clicking a complex canvas, though the core simulator is usable manually.
leverage_evidence: Description claims 33 WebMCP tools covering the studio.
Tools operate on graph topology, simulation parameters, provider comparison, and meters.
execution_rationale: The concept is unusually complete on paper—traffic classes, gates, quotas, timelines, billing sources, and comparison—but the evidence packet lacks legible end-to-end proof.
execution_evidence: Demo marked alive.
Pitch specifies conservation of arrivals and served/blocked/dropped outcomes plus provider pricing URLs.
Frame sheet shows a dark build/workspace UI with prompt and populated project panels.
impact_rationale: Developers and teams genuinely need pre-build cost and quota validation; making the architecture itself executable provides credible value.
impact_evidence: Targets recurring pricing-tab and first-invoice uncertainty.
Compares Cloudflare/Vercel and exposes source-backed meters.
creativity_rationale: Treating a network diagram as a runnable economic simulator, then letting an agent co-design it, is a fresh synthesis pursued at ambitious scope.
creativity_evidence: Traffic sources include humans, crawlers, scrapers, and botnets.
Timeline shows which layer breaks and when.
usability_note: Canvas plus simulation is legible, though many provider and meter concepts could be dense.
red_flags: Frame text is too small to verify detailed simulation claims.
standouts: Architecture drawing doubles as executable cost model.
advance_reason: Strong developer value and original simulator concept; deserves advancement despite thin visual proof.

one_line: Asymmetric escape-room game where a human sees visual clues and an AI agent operates remote systems through WebMCP.
what_it_does: Pairs player-only visual information with agent-only facility manual/tools; progress requires exchanging information to solve randomized puzzles and escape.
leverage_rationale: The agent tool boundary is the game mechanic: structured access intentionally partitions knowledge and capabilities, making WebMCP central rather than decorative.
leverage_evidence: Eight tools expose only manual, system state, decoding, remote operations, and release actions.
Player cannot access remote systems and Relay cannot see the room.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a coherent playable loop with stages, randomized puzzles, scoring, persistence, voice, offline mode, and a one-level scope; the frame sheet visibly shows narrative progression and branching choices.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows opening and later story states with numbered choices.
Demo marked alive; installable PWA and saved progress are claimed.
impact_rationale: The audience is players seeking cooperative puzzle play, and the asymmetric human-agent design credibly creates a novel social/game experience.
impact_evidence: Pitch directly defines cooperative escape-room audience and goal.
Visual sequence shows a playable narrative/choice flow.
creativity_rationale: Making the WebMCP information boundary itself an asymmetric escape-room role is genuinely novel and memorable.
creativity_evidence: Human and agent have deliberately complementary senses and permissions.
Puzzle progress depends on communication through the agent.
usability_note: Clear role separation, but setup across compatible WebMCP clients may add friction.
red_flags: Only one simple level is included; agent invocation itself is not clearly visible in the contact sheet.
standouts: WebMCP is the core interaction design.
advance_reason: Exceptional creativity and transformative WebMCP use in a coherent game loop.

one_line: Checksum-bound preference passport carried across stores to produce explainable, reversible shopping decisions.
what_it_does: Captures explicit likes/dislikes, lets users edit rules, ranks sample products, asks the smallest decisive question, and emits a receipt with counterfactuals.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP carries exact human-approved structured state across origins and exposes only valid next actions, improving reliability and auditability beyond UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Description emphasizes checksum-bound envelope and cross-store handoff.
Dynamic registration exposes next valid tool and preserves E01-E04 evidence trace.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a tightly specified multi-stage journey with editable evidence, deterministic ranking, a reversal case, and final receipt; visual evidence is limited to a contact sheet.
execution_evidence: Named Form House, Common Room, One Question Engine, and Decision Receipt stages.
24-to-3 shortlist and H01 reversal are concrete test cases.
impact_rationale: Shoppers and recommendation users have a real problem with opaque cross-store trade-offs; explicit preference ownership and explanations offer credible value.
impact_evidence: Targets fragmented preferences and unexplained recommendations.
Receipt explains winner, losses, accepted trade-off, and reversal.
creativity_rationale: The checksum-bound preference artifact and minimal-question/counterfactual decision model are original extensions of agentic shopping.
creativity_evidence: Agent must stop and ask a human-owned question when ranking can change.
Evidence remains visible through cross-origin handoff.
usability_note: Staged workflow and editable rules support trust, though terminology is somewhat novel.
red_flags: Fictional sample chairs and no transcript limit observed proof.
standouts: Human-approved state is preserved across stores.
advance_reason: Highly coherent, differentiated agent-shopping workflow with strong trust mechanics.

one_line: Parametric 3D pottery editor that turns agent-generated forms into deterministic multi-page clay templates.
what_it_does: Lets humans and agents adjust vessel parameters, sync paired browsers, preview geometry, and export precise printable templates with undo/redo.
leverage_rationale: The agent handles high-level geometric intent while the app deterministically produces exact fabrication geometry, solving a precision gap general agents handle poorly.
leverage_evidence: Transcript explicitly contrasts nondeterministic AI templates with deterministic app output.
Agent sends parameters and software generates matching multi-page templates.
execution_rationale: The 179-second video transcript describes live connection, parameter change, synchronization, and reversible edits; frame sheet visibly shows repeated 3D editor states and a document/template view.
execution_evidence: Video is present and transcript reports an agent change arriving in under a second.
Frame sheet shows shaded/wireframe pottery geometry and document/template views.
About text claims printable multi-page PDF export.
impact_rationale: Potters have a specific costly failure mode—misaligned templates discovered after studio work—and deterministic output directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Target audience and cereal-box/template workflow are concrete.
Undo/redo and precise printable output support practical use.
creativity_rationale: The human-agent division between creative shape exploration and deterministic physical fabrication is an inventive, well-pursued interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Paired browser/WebSocket workflow bridges agent and editor.
Design initiated by agent or Chrome tab is shown as a core feature.
usability_note: Direct parameter editing, paired-browser access, and undo/redo make the precision workflow approachable.
red_flags: Only a limited number of tools are visible in the packaging; export correctness is claimed rather than independently checked.
standouts: Physical-world output is deterministic and reversible.
advance_reason: Strong demonstrated execution, clear audience pain, and unusually effective WebMCP/product boundary.

one_line: Shared evidence board for searching public comments, verifying excerpts, and producing traceable briefs.
what_it_does: Agents search Regulations.gov and pin candidate excerpts; analysts verify or remove evidence before a cited brief is exported.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP connects agent search/pinning to live analyst-reviewed state and prevents unreviewed evidence from entering exports, a meaningful reliability delta over chat/UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies agent reads analyst decisions and shared evidence board.
Quote validation and export gating are explicit challenges/features.
execution_rationale: The workflow is coherent and demo is alive, but no frame sheets or video were submitted, so end-to-end visual execution cannot be verified and score is capped.
execution_evidence: Live demo URL and stack are provided.
About text describes pagination, quote validation, review, and cited brief.
impact_rationale: Policy researchers and analysts face a real scale-and-traceability problem in public comments; source-linked review directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: Specific Regulations.gov research workflow.
Analyst verification and cited exports are central.
creativity_rationale: Human review of agent-collected regulatory evidence is a strong synthesis, though the research-board category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Unreviewed evidence is explicitly excluded from exports.
Agent and analyst decisions remain shared and visible.
usability_note: Traceability is well designed conceptually; dense evidence review may require careful information architecture.
red_flags: No video frame sheets or video; visual claims cannot be checked.
advance_reason: Credible high-value research workflow, with execution confidence reduced by absent visual evidence.

one_line: Attributed deliberation rooms where humans and agents propose, amend, second, object, and ratify civic ideas.
what_it_does: Provides deterministic quorum and objection rules, revision history, source attribution, and human-only ratification for civic proposals.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools make attribution, amendments, quorum, and shared deliberation state explicit and auditable; generic UI automation would be less dependable for these constraints.
leverage_evidence: WebMCP integration is built with webmcp-react and shared room state.
AI can build consensus but cannot ratify; deterministic rules enforce this.
execution_rationale: The packet specifies a complete deliberation state machine and the frame sheet shows a dark civic interface, but end-to-end agent action is not visibly proven.
execution_evidence: Rules require at least 3 seconds and more seconds than objections.
Frame sheet shows repeated room/proposal states and attributed discussion UI.
impact_rationale: Civic groups and deliberative communities have a real need for less reactive, more accountable decision processes; the explicit rules address forum failure modes.
impact_evidence: Targets engagement-driven forums and buried ideas.
Human-only ratification protects decision authority.
creativity_rationale: Treating amendment, attribution, quorum, and model identity as first-class interaction primitives is a thoughtful and original civic design.
creativity_evidence: AI model and agent ID are shown on contributions.
Consensus is deterministic rather than upvote/moderator dependent.
usability_note: Explicit actions clarify deliberation, though quorum mechanics may need onboarding.
red_flags: No transcript and limited gallery mean actual agent collaboration is not fully observable.
standouts: Strong accountability model for AI participation.
advance_reason: Original civic interaction model with credible social value and clear guardrails.

one_line: Infinite connected canvas where people and agents plan, trace systems, attach evidence, and learn without losing context.
what_it_does: Supports build, trace, and learn maps with linked nodes, plans, evidence, comments, locks, selected-context focus, and quizzes.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP provides structured access to selected nodes, relationships, evidence, and map operations, materially reducing context loss versus chat plus manual copying.
leverage_evidence: 15 WebMCP tools read context, create maps, update plans, add evidence, and focus paths.
Inspector and human-controlled locks make agent work reviewable.
execution_rationale: The product scope is broad but internally coherent, and the frame sheet shows a dark workspace progressing from build prompt to populated code/workflow-like panels; details are small.
execution_evidence: Demo marked alive and public repository exists.
Description gives concrete Build/Trace/Learn map behaviors and example flow.
impact_rationale: Teams, researchers, and learners routinely lose relationships and evidence in chat; a persistent connected workspace directly addresses that need.
impact_evidence: Specific roadmap, user-journey, and learning-map use cases.
Human locks and linked evidence support trust.
creativity_rationale: Connected planning plus tracing and learning is a useful synthesis with a clear context-preservation angle, though canvas products are established.
creativity_evidence: Three map modes share one agent-readable workspace.
Selected-node Trace action is a concrete collaboration pattern.
usability_note: Persistent visual context is helpful; three modes and many tools risk cognitive load.
red_flags: Broad scope and small frame text make completeness difficult to verify.
standouts: Agent work remains inspectable and lockable.
advance_reason: Solid context-preserving product with broad credible utility and meaningful structured-agent delta.

one_line: Real Italian business website augmented with an agent-facing layer for service understanding and safely prepared customer actions.
what_it_does: Exposes structured business knowledge, services, constraints, and contact/assistance actions alongside the existing Joomla site, with human confirmation.
leverage_rationale: The business itself exposes authoritative service semantics and constraints directly, avoiding brittle DOM interpretation and making agent recommendations/action preparation more reliable.
leverage_evidence: Agent Interface Layer is described as alongside the human interface.
Workflow is website knowledge to agent reasoning to human confirmation to safe action.
execution_rationale: The packet is coherent and grounded in a live production site, but no video and no readable frame analysis were available to verify the full workflow.
execution_evidence: Real Show Room La Finestra Joomla website is identified as pre-existing.
Demo marked alive; five gallery images listed.
Description names concrete service domains and safe-action boundary.
impact_rationale: Customers with location- and service-specific needs benefit from agents that can understand real business offerings and prepare contact requests safely.
impact_evidence: Concrete example: stuck security door in Ceprano.
Targets real customers and an existing operating business.
creativity_rationale: Making an existing local business website speak directly to agents is practical and well-motivated, though the agent-ready-site pattern is emerging rather than wholly novel.
creativity_evidence: Applies WebMCP to a real pre-existing production site, not a simulated storefront.
Combines structured knowledge with human-confirmed action.
usability_note: Preserving the familiar website while adding an agent layer is a strong adoption-oriented choice.
red_flags: Project explicitly integrates a pre-existing site; challenge-newness of the underlying product is limited.
advance_reason: Credible real-world deployment pattern with strong practical impact, despite limited observable proof.

one_line: Agent-native storefront where shoppers and agents share a session, with UI grounding and human-gated checkout.
what_it_does: Provides catalog browsing, cart operations, discounts, and agent assistance while requiring deliberate human confirmation before placing an order.
leverage_rationale: Shared cart/session state and structured catalog/checkout tools improve agent reliability, but a competent general agent could achieve much of the same shopping outcome through the visible UI.
leverage_evidence: Pitch claims entire storefront architecture exposed via WebMCP.
Human sign-off gate and live UI grounding are central features.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a plausible complete shopping flow and many gallery assets, but the supplied evidence is mostly packaging text with no video and no legible workflow verification.
execution_evidence: Eight gallery images are listed and demo marked alive.
Description names shoes/jackets, cart, agent work, checkout request, and confirmation states.
impact_rationale: Shoppers and merchants have a real need for safe delegation of repetitive product discovery while preserving payment consent; value is credible though generic.
impact_evidence: Explicit 90% autonomous shopping versus final human sign-off framing.
Catalog, comparison, discount, cart, and checkout use cases are concrete.
creativity_rationale: The shared-session and secure human-gated checkout are useful refinements of agentic commerce, but the storefront concept itself is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Live UI grounding and checkout validation are highlighted.
Agent and shopper collaborate in one session.
usability_note: Human confirmation improves trust; storefront copy and polish appear less consistent in the packet text.
red_flags: Packet text is noisy/duplicated and contains visible spelling errors; no video transcript.
Actual checkout completion is not independently observable.
advance_reason: Credible but comparatively familiar commerce concept with thin execution evidence and only meaningful WebMCP delta.
